*Settling in to think this through as the farmer himself*

---

My name doesn't matter — let me just tell you how I'm thinking about this year.

I'm 48, middle school finished, and honestly I've only been back on the land two years. Before that I was working construction outside the province. My old mother still lives with us and my wife does most of the vegetable work with me. Three of us in the household, 10.1 mu to manage. It's not much land, so every mu has to earn.

I split my land three ways. About **5.6 mu** is my wheat-maize ground — that's the food and the safety net. If vegetables fail, at least we have grain to sell or eat. Then **3 mu** is eggplant (that's my money crop, Old Wang next door has been doing eggplant twenty years and he's been teaching me), and **1.5 mu** is chili. I keep vegetables on separate plots from the wheat-maize because the watering and the work schedule are totally different.

**Wheat (5.6 mu).** I planted already back in October. I put down about 40 kg of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) per mu before sowing, which comes to maybe 6 kg N per mu at the base. Come spring when it jointing, I'll topdress about 15 kg of urea per mu — so roughly 13 kg more N. That's around 19 kg N total per mu. I know the extension guy last year said 15 kg N is enough, but I'd rather be a little heavy than see it turn yellow in April. Last year I got about 420 kg/mu, which is fine for our conditions. I'll irrigate three times — at greening, jointing, and grain-filling. Well water costs me, but without those three waterings the yield drops fast on this soil.

**Maize (5.6 mu).** Right after wheat harvest in mid-June, I've got about a week to get maize in. Very tight. I buy Zhengdan 958 seed or whatever the agri-supply shop recommends — hybrid, about 50 yuan per mu for seed. I no-till straight into the wheat stubble, the custom planter guy comes through the village and charges 30 yuan per mu. I apply about 40 kg of compound fertilizer at planting and then topdress 10-12 kg urea at the big trumpet stage. One irrigation if it's dry in July, sometimes two. Expect around 450 kg/mu.

**Eggplant (3 mu).** This is where I spend my money. I buy seedlings from the market in late April — about 2,000 seedlings per mu at 0.15 yuan each. I lay plastic mulch (the black kind, cheap), put down about 2 tons of chicken manure per mu before planting (300 yuan/ton from the chicken farm outside the village), then 50 kg of compound fertilizer per mu. Through the season I topdress urea and potassium sulfate four or five times — maybe 25-30 kg N/mu total for the year because eggplant is hungry and you pick from it for months. I irrigate through a flexible hose from the well — probably 8-10 times across the season, whenever the leaves start drooping. Trellising is labor. My wife and I put in maybe 60 days each on the eggplant. I hire two neighbors for a few days at transplant and at peak picking, 100 yuan per day each. I spray for flea beetles and red spider mite — I watch my neighbor's field, when he sprays I usually spray too. Expect around 4,000-5,000 kg/mu if the market holds. If prices crash in August like they did two years ago, I just keep picking what I can sell and feed the rest to the chickens.

**Chili (1.5 mu).** Similar to eggplant but less demanding. Seedlings in late April, about 3,000 per mu. Chicken manure base, compound fertilizer, and two or three topdresses through summer — about 20 kg N/mu total. Irrigate maybe 6-7 times. Main worry is anthracnose if it rains a lot in August — I spray preventively with mancozeb a couple of times. Expected yield around 2,500 kg/mu of fresh chili, or I dry some of it if the fresh price is bad.

**What I'm worrying about this year.** Urea went up again last autumn. Diesel for the pump is not cheap either. I'd like to put on more fertilizer on the eggplant but my cash is tied up in seedlings and mulch in April-May. I'll go to the village credit co-op if I need to for the summer topdress. I'm not going to change anything big this year — last year worked out okay and with only two years under my belt I'm not going to experiment. Maybe in another year or two, if I see somebody doing something smart, I'll try it on a small strip first.
